feasibility_reasoning:
The harness works and its gates are green. I ran these read-only:
- `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json`: 0 errors.
- `eslint scripts/performance/`: clean.
- `prettier --check` on all 12 files: clean.
- `node --test document-weight.test.mjs`: 7/7.
- `node scripts/performance/check-document-weight.ts`: "✓ Waga dokumentu w progach".

No product code is touched, so the SSR, chunk, entry-purity and loader gates cannot regress. `check:gate-coverage` only reads package.json scripts (scripts/check-gate-coverage.ts:33-36), and vitest only includes `src/**` (vitest.config.ts:9).

The fidelity claims are overstated, though.

(1) The cached document goes STALE mid-series, and nothing controls it.
- DOCUMENT_CACHE_MAX_FRESH_MS=180000 (src/lib/http/documentCache.ts:47,269), but the harness warms each artifact only once (lighthouse-local.mjs:333).
- The workstream's own server logs show STALE plus a background re-render during measured runs: ab-h1-h2 A 4x / B 2x (asymmetric), ab-js-lowprio 3x/3x, baseline-h2 4x.
- That re-render runs in the same Node process that serves all assets (one origin), on the shared CPU.
- The revalidator (src/server.ts:203) re-renders with Lighthouse's own UA. LH 13 does not add "Chrome-Lighthouse" (lighthouse core/config/constants.js:43), so `isbot` is false and the cache flips to the streaming variant. `--warm-ua bot` is therefore only valid for about the first 3 minutes.

(2) The "PSI-identical" variant is not established.
- `isbot` is true for "...Chrome-Lighthouse" (verified).
- TanStack waits for allReady for bots (node_modules/@tanstack/react-router/dist/esm/ssr/renderRouterToStream.js:31).
- PSI appends Chrome-Lighthouse, so on a MISS PSI gets the buffered bot variant. A browser warm-up measures what users get on a HIT, not necessarily what PSI gets.

(3) psi-sample.mjs:71 builds params without `locale=pl`. PSI then defaults to en, and src/start.ts homepageLangMiddleware (~138-148) answers 302 to /en, so the sampler measures a different page. This contradicts EVIDENCE §0-cloud.

(4) The noise floor did not come from an A/A run. In ab-js-lowprio, side B had a transform: the document was buffered and recompressed, and 44 attributes were injected. B's main thread was higher in every pair (10257/8199/10838 vs 8694/5903/6316 ms), which is systematic, not noise.

(5) Request count drifts by run index the same way on both sides (122, then 134/148, then 182). The cause is client refetches to the dead 127.0.0.1:4199 (/rest/v1/posts x24 in run 3), likely tied to document age vs staleTime 5 min (src/router.tsx:46). Interleaving cancels this in A/B, but a single-artifact DELTA against the baseline JSON does not.

Minor:
- The type-stripping note is wrong: it is on by default only from Node 22.18/23.6.
- `highPriorityBytesBeforeLcpImage` counts requests that start before the image ends, using observed timings. It is a proxy, not deterministic.
blocking_issues: psi-sample.mjs:71 sends no locale=pl. PSI defaults to en, gets 302 to /en (src/start.ts homepageLangMiddleware) and measures a different page than the contract PSI run. Add params.set('locale','pl') and assert finalPath === '/'.

Single warm-up (lighthouse-local.mjs:333) vs the 3-min fresh window (documentCache.ts:47). STALE background re-renders happen during measured runs, asymmetrically between A and B (ab-h1-h2 A 4x vs B 2x). They re-seed the browser variant, so --warm-ua bot is invalid after about 3 min. Re-warm with the chosen UA before every run.

The 'A/A' noise floor came from ab-js-lowprio, whose B side carried a transform (buffered and recompressed document, 44 injected attributes) and had higher main-thread time in every pair. Run a real A/A (--compare . . with no transform, n>=5) before using TBT ±464 ms or perf -13 as the noise floor.

The 'PSI-identical' claim is wrong for the document variant. PSI's UA contains Chrome-Lighthouse, so isbot is true and PSI gets the buffered variant on a MISS. Label the default browser-warm mode as the user/HIT variant, or report a --warm-ua A/B.
effect_reasoning:
This is a tool, so the direct Lighthouse score effect is 0. Bias corrections, checked per pair in ab-h1-h2.log:

h2 vs h1:
- Mobile LCP: 4.02→3.63, 5.12→4.99, 5.55→4.82. Pair 3 changes FCP mode (5.00 vs 4.07 s), so the same-mode delta is −0.13 to −0.39 s. The −0.30 s median holds within about ±0.15 s.
- Desktop FCP: 1.09→0.84, 1.14→0.79, 1.10→0.82, i.e. −0.25 to −0.35 s, consistent with the claim.

Converted to score with the LH curves:
- Mobile LCP (median 4000, p10 2500, σ 0.367): 5.12 s scores 0.25 and 4.82 s scores 0.305, so +0.055 x 25 = about +1.4 pts. The logged +9 is TBT noise.
- Desktop FCP (σ 0.42): 1.10 s scores 0.81 and 0.82 s about 0.94, so +1.3 pts.
- Desktop LCP (σ 0.541): 1.24 s scores 0.889 and 0.94 s scores 0.958, so +1.7 pts.
- Desktop total is about +3, matching 95→98.

The bot-variant bias was measured only in bytes (382 vs 391 KB, 14 vs 22 scripts). There is no Lighthouse A/B of bot-warm vs browser-warm, so its effect on the metrics is unquantified.

The noise claim is weaker than stated. The FCP/LCP ±0.01 s figure is one n=3 pair, and mobile FCP is bimodal (2.9 vs 4.1 s; about 3% chance that an n=3 median changes mode). The TBT noise floor is unknown because the 'A/A' had a treatment.

The remaining gaps to PSI are larger than the biases removed:
- local HIT TTFB is 11 ms vs prod MISS 2.75 s, about +2.6 s on simulated FCP/LCP
- the fixture document is 391 KB vs 569 KB in prod
- client fetches fail locally but succeed in prod, so TBT work differs
- Chrome 141 locally vs PSI's Chrome

So the harness is valid for paired A/B deltas only, not as an absolute PSI predictor. A cheaper way to the same fidelity is three small fixes inside M1, not a new tool: re-warm per run, add locale=pl, and run a real A/A.
corrected_estimate: Lighthouse score: 0 pts (measurement only). The old harness's bias is smaller than "+0.30 s LCP / +0.28 s FCP" suggests in score terms: h2 vs h1 is mobile LCP −0.30 s ±0.15 s (same-mode pairs −0.13 to −0.39 s), about +1.4 mobile pts (TBT excluded), and desktop FCP −0.25 to −0.35 s / LCP −0.30 s, about +3 desktop pts. The bot-variant bias is unquantified in Lighthouse metrics (bytes only). The noise floor is FCP/LCP ±0.01 s only when both sides land in the same FCP mode (bimodal, about 1.1 s jumps); the TBT/perf noise floor is unestablished until a real A/A is run.
better_alternative: Keep M1, with three fixes. (1) Re-warm the document with the chosen UA right before each Lighthouse run, so no STALE revalidation happens inside a run and the bot variant stays pinned. (2) Add locale=pl to psi-sample.mjs and treat finalPath != '/' as an error. (3) Run a true A/A (--compare . . with no transform, n>=5 per form) and record it as the noise floor. Also add a --warm-ua bot vs browser A/B so the variant effect is measured in Lighthouse metrics, and log x-nes-cache per run.
